threat_event: Attacker takes over a site management dashboard account and pushes a malicious plugin to all 120 connected customer sites (payment-page skimmer on online stores, rogue administrator users, spam pages)
threat_source: Cybercriminal group (credential phishing or infostealer malware on a contractor laptop)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Freelance developer's administrator account has no MFA and is used from a personal laptop; any account can upload code to many sites at once; activity log never reviewed; former contractor account was still active
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-04 dashboard; 120 care-plan sites; BP-01; BP-04
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 2, 3, 5); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2), (6)(a)
existing_controls: Owner's dashboard account uses MFA; weekly bulk updates; daily scans of all sites
treatment_plan: Require MFA on every dashboard account; freelancer limited to assigned sites with no package upload or bulk actions; only the owner pushes code to more than one site; weekly activity log review; security terms for the freelancer; P08 runbook

threat_event: Attacker phishes the customer portal administrator password and uses the stored API credentials to terminate hosting accounts, redirect domains, or demand a ransom
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Portal administrator login uses a password only; the portal holds API credentials with full control of SYS-02 and SYS-03; upstream backups are deleted with a terminated account
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-01 portal; SYS-02; SYS-03; BP-01; BP-03
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 3); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)
existing_controls: Unique generated password in the password manager; registrar lock on
treatment_plan: Turn on portal MFA now and add a security key by 2027-03-31; ask the upstream provider for an API key that cannot terminate accounts; independent backups (R-005); registrar lock on every domain

threat_event: Theft of the customer password spreadsheet or of emailed credentials leads to takeover of many customer sites and SFTP accounts
threat_source: Cybercriminal (cloud storage or email account compromise; compromise of the freelancer's mailbox)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: About 140 site and SFTP passwords in a readable spreadsheet; credentials sent by plain email to customers and the freelancer; older site passwords followed a pattern
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-06 file storage and email; customer sites
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 3); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)
existing_controls: Email and file storage protected by MFA
treatment_plan: Move every customer credential into a shared password manager vault; rotate all 140 passwords; share credentials only through the vault; delete the spreadsheet and the emailed copies

threat_event: Automated mass exploitation of known-vulnerable plugins on hosting-only sites infects customer sites; the upstream provider suspends the reseller account for abuse, taking every customer offline
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Nobody patches the 150 hosting-only sites; 64 ran a vulnerable plugin in August 2026; Terms of Service do not assign patching; a 2025 defacement and a 2026 web shell came from this gap
affected_asset_or_process: Hosting-only sites; SYS-02 reseller account; BP-01
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 9); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)
existing_controls: Daily vulnerability scans; server-level malware scanning by the upstream provider
treatment_plan: Notify each hosting-only customer of open vulnerabilities monthly; offer automatic security updates at no charge; update the Terms of Service to state patching duty and the right to suspend a vulnerable site; firewall rules from the security service on stores

threat_event: Customer sites and mail are lost for good after an upstream platform failure, a malicious account deletion, or ransomware on a shared server
threat_source: Upstream provider failure or attacker with control plane access
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 235 of 270 sites have only the upstream backup: 7 days, same provider, deleted with the account; owner restore tested once (2026-08-19)
affected_asset_or_process: All customer sites and mailboxes; BP-01
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 deception (45(a); website: 30-day backups); FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 4)
existing_controls: Upstream nightly backups (7 days); dashboard backups for 35 premium sites
treatment_plan: Independent daily off-site backups for every site and mailbox with 30-day retention; quarterly restore tests of 3 sites; monthly DNS zone export

threat_event: Customers or a regulator challenge public security claims that are not true (30-day backups, malware protection on every site, data never leaves the USA, 99.9% uptime)
threat_source: Regulator or customer (complaint after an incident)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Website and questionnaire answers written from assumptions; no substantiation file
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 deception (45(a); website and questionnaire answers)
treatment_plan: Correct the website and questionnaire answers to match what is true today; keep a substantiation file for each claim; restore the claims only when the controls exist

threat_event: A customer data breach is not reported to the customer within 10 days, or the customer lacks the facts it needs for its own notices
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident plan, no customer security contact list, owner unaware of the third-party agent duty; the 2026-08-05 determination was not documented; dashboard log kept 30 days
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Data Breach Response guide)
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook and notice templates; collect a security contact for every customer; document every breach determination; export logs monthly

threat_event: AI alert triage dismisses a real compromise, so an attacker stays on customer sites undetected
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Auto-dismiss is on with no human review; a web shell was dismissed on 2026-07-21 and found on 2026-08-05; 58% of July findings auto-dismissed
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 5); FTC Act Sec. 5 deception (45(a); website: malware protection)
treatment_plan: Turn off auto-dismiss for new administrator users and changed executable files; owner reviews dismissed findings weekly; sample 50 dismissals a month (P10)

threat_event: Owner is suddenly unavailable or loses the only phone, so nobody can run support, renew domains, or restore customer services
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One person holds every role and credential; all second factors on one phone; recovery codes not offline; no backup operator
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 4); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a)
treatment_plan: Sealed emergency access envelope with the owner's attorney; written backup-operator arrangement; offline customer contact list; ask the upstream provider and registrar about designated-person access (P05)

threat_event: The upstream provider has a long outage, ends its reseller program, or goes out of business
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single upstream provider; no tested migration path; reseller terms allow program changes on 30 days' notice
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 8)
treatment_plan: Independent backups (R-005) double as a migration path; document a migration runbook to a second provider; review the upstream SOC 2 report every year

threat_event: Customer personal information and site credentials pasted into a consumer AI chat assistant are kept or used for training
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Free consumer account; no data rules for AI tools; pasted log excerpts with shopper emails and IP addresses, and a configuration file with a database password
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 1); FTC Act Sec. 5 deception (45(a); Terms of Service confidentiality)
treatment_plan: Stop pasting customer data; redact before any use; rotate the exposed database password; use only an approved business-tier tool with no-training terms (P10)

threat_event: A former contractor, or anyone holding a former contractor's credentials, uses a forgotten account to reach customer sites
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No account review or removal step when an engagement ends; a former freelance designer's dashboard account (engagement ended 2025-11) was active until 2026-08-19 (P07 finding)
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 2)
treatment_plan: Account disabled 2026-08-19; monthly account review of every control plane tool; removal the day an engagement ends; check the account's 30-day activity log and the affected sites

threat_event: Theft or loss of the owner's laptop or phone
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptop travels; phone holds every second factor
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 10)
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; phone passcode; MFA everywhere
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Laptop is encrypted and phone has a passcode; recovery codes go in the emergency envelope (R-009); turn on remote wipe

threat_event: Hurricane or a long power and internet outage at the home office
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. All services are cloud-hosted; the owner works from the phone hotspot or relocates with the laptop and phone when a storm watch is issued

threat_event: FTC or Florida Attorney General action, or customer claims, after a breach because no documented reasonable security program existed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written policies, risk assessment, or vendor oversight before 2026-09-28
regulatory_driver: FTC Act Sec. 5 (45(n); Start with Security 1-10); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2), (9)
treatment_plan: Keep this register and POL-01 current; review every August and after changes; keep records 5 years
